newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Australia, Singapore boost air links.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Singapore boost air links.

text.p: Australia and Singapore announced an agreement to boost air links between the two countries on Thursday.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore said in a statement "the new arrangements included a 37.5 percent increase in passenger service capacity for the airlines of both sides up the year 1999".
This would mean an increase equivalent to an extra 15 Boeing 747 services per week for each side.
The CAAS said the agreement would also more than double freighter flights from 4.5 to 12 Boeing 747 services per week.
"The new arrangements will benefit Singapore Airlines and Qantas, which are the only Singapore and Australian carriers operating the route for the time being," the CAAS statement said.

Asked what the deal meant in financial terms, visiting Australian Prime Minister John Howard told reporters it was "difficult to quantify", but that anything which doubled freighter services was bound to be significant.
Howard, on a two-day visit to Singapore, was speaking after a meeting with Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong.
Singapore recently announced open skies pacts with New Zealand and the United States to improve a traffic flows and air services.
